speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when your symptoms started and specifically where you feel the pain in your side?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your symptoms persisted after the sinusitis improved, were the flank pains accompanied by chills, and did you notice any changes in your urine such as blood or cloudiness?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine_Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows Leukocyturia (Present) and Cytospin-Stained-With-Hansel's-Solution revealing 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Urine_Culture is Negative.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyelonephritis.

While the patient mentions a rash resolving with a medication change (suggesting a possible drug reaction or Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction), the clinical picture of persistent fever and flank pain after sinusitis treatment, combined with the provider's prior assessment, strongly supports a diagnosis of pyelonephritis. I have already requested a Urinalysis and Urine Culture to confirm this.
